 Hantavirus — Lessons Learned about Security and Solidarity 
 P. Sánchez and T.A. Ghebreyesus

 Beyond Percentage of Weight Lost — Protecting Participants in Obesity Trials 
 S.H. Schmitz
 The efficacy and popularity of GLP-1 agents have sparked a race to develop increasingly potent therapies. But protections for people enrolled in trials of investigational products may be inadequate. Read the article. 
 PERSPECTIVE
 Grief as a Vector for Disease — Tradition and Public Health in Ebola Outbreaks 
 C. Mutuyimana and C. Killikelly
 When public health measures conflict with cultural, relational, and emotional practices surrounding severe illness and death, they may lead to uprisings that increase the risk of infection spread. Read the article. 
 PERSPECTIVE
 A Guide for the Perplexed Physician 
 D. Ariel
 As access to medical knowledge is democratized, the specialist’s position atop the medical hierarchy grows shaky. With integration and synthesis more precious than ever, the generalist deserves reappraisal. Read the article.

 E.L. Mayer and Others
 In ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, giredestrant, an ER degrader and full ER antagonist, plus everolimus led to longer progression-free survival than standard endocrine therapy–everolimus; safety was similar. Read the article.

 Opioid-Settlement Funds — Lessons from Tobacco 
 B.D. Scher and H.H. Howard
 Settlements of lawsuits against opioid manufacturers and other entities will shape drug policy for decades. Attention is needed to ensure that the funds will be dedicated to evidence-based activities. Read the article.
